A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AnyMC3D study. All 19 pages, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–H, are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification experiments across 12 tasks, baseline comparisons, ablations, calibration experiments and trauma subgroup analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and additionally tabulates per-finding CT-RATE AUCs in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The LoRA adaptation, query-based slice aggregation, multi-view fusion, auxiliary segmentation, heatmap generation and challenge calibration/ensembling procedures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 12 tasks and datasets. The added CT-RATE table covers the same 18 abnormalities already evaluated in Figure 3.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout. In particular, CT-RATE still compares against CT-Net and CT-CLIP's ClassFine variant; the revised CT-CLIP score does not introduce a different baseline.

E3.justification: v3 specifies an official CT-RATE split of 47,149 training and 3,039 validation volumes. However, Table 3 in both versions lists 45,149 training, 2,000 validation and 3,039 test volumes. The PDFs do not clarify whether the added wording describes official versus internal partitions or a changed training/evaluation protocol. Other stated settings are retained.

E4.justification: The decoder, adaptation, data-size, calibration, slice-fusion, backbone-size, DINO-version, heatmap and trauma subgroup analyses are retained. The new per-finding CT-RATE table documents existing benchmark performance rather than adding an analytical experiment.

E5.justification: No new seeds, repeated-run estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests accompany the revised results. The existing 10-model ensemble description is unchanged.

E6.justification: Section 4.2 revises CT-CLIP's reported mean AUC from 0.768 to 0.748 and AnyMC3D (DINOv2) from 0.882 to 0.884; CT-Net remains 0.631. New Table 5 supplies exact AUCs for the 18 findings already plotted in Figure 3. These are limited reporting changes; the PDFs do not establish a rerun or a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations 1–12 are retained. No definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning scalable adaptation, the 12-task benchmark, general-purpose 2D foundation models and first place in VLM3D.

C2.justification: The explanations of adaptation and pretraining effects, 2D versus 3D performance, and clinical heatmaps are unchanged. The limitations concerning evaluated models, in-domain CT/MRI data and costly pixel-level supervision are also retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds explicit official CT-RATE split sizes and identifies Table 5 results as official-validation AUCs. This expands experimental documentation, although its relationship to Table 3 remains unexplained. Implementation details, hyperparameters and access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive positioning against prior foundation-model and 3D classification research are unchanged, including the challenge-solution discussion in Appendix E.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized edits to the CT-RATE passage, adds a short per-finding-results paragraph in Appendix D and updates cross-references. The overall section organization and narrative are retained.

P2.justification: v3 inserts Table 5, renumbers the former Tables 5–8 as Tables 6–9, and reflows nearby appendix material, including Figures 9–10. Existing plots and previously reported tables are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: New Table 5 makes the existing CT-RATE results easier to check and reuse; its 18 AUCs average to the revised 0.884. This provides a modest improvement in reporting precision. The gain is limited by the unexplained relationship between the new split description in Section 4.2 and the unchanged Table 3.
